newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Bank predicts drop in ZCCM export earnings.
newsitem.headline: Bank predicts drop in ZCCM export earnings.

text.p: Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines's (ZCCM) export earnings in 1996 are likely to drop by a third from 1995 due to lower production and depressed copper prices, a recent Barclays Bank of Zambia report said.

The bank said in the report released this week that periodic production breakdowns and low metal prices in the year had adversely affected ZCCM's export earnings -- which makes up around 90 percent of Zambia's foreign exchange earnings.

"The low production and reduced metal prices will adversely affect foreign exchange earnings by ZCCM. It is projected that earnings by ZCCM in 1996 will decline by about 33 percent to $756 million compared to $1.1 billion in 1995," the report says.
ZCCM suffered production breakdowns with the shutdown of the Nkana smelter, a fire accident at Mufulira smelter and a miners' strike at Nchanga division during the year.
In October, production fell to a record low of 18,330 tonnes, affecting the company's prospects of meeting its production target of 335,000 tonnes in the year.
Cobalt production fell to about 289 tonnes in October from 499 tonnes the previous month.
The decline in copper earnings came at a time when Western donors had cut aid to Zambia in the run-up to controversial general elections last November.
ZCCM is up for sale under an ambitious privatisation exercise of state-run enterprises, many of which have been performing badly.
Detailed bids for the company's assets will be made in February, and offers are likely to be made to successful bidders in the third quarter of the year.
